title: Nilus
summary: Egyptian king. Shuckford places the start of his reign 436 years before the first Olympiad, following Dicaearchus, and calls him the thirty-sixth king from Menes in the canon of Eratosthenes.
description: Added from the Shuckford import. Display only. Shuckford’s years are Anno Mundi, or a “years before Christ” figure he is reporting. This chronology never sets a sort, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person’s birth, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Shuckford is display-only).

reign.date: the reign of Nilus therefore began A. M. 2792
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 186 (facsimile PDF p. 282)
reign.note: From Dicaearchus’s 436 years before the first Olympiad, and from Ussher’s A. M. 3228 for that Olympiad. Both numbers are printed. He also says Eratosthenes makes Nilus the thirty-sixth king from Menes.
